description: A pattern sequencer of eight lines, each holding a text expression: written as a clock expression it makes a rhythm, written as a pitch expression it makes a melody

params.text: Switches that line between a clock expression, which puts out triggers, and a pitch expression, which puts out volt-per-octave pitches
Leans the random sequence types towards the lower values in a sequence turned one way and towards the higher ones turned the other; centred they are even

inputs.text: A rising edge sends every line's expression back to its beginning
A rising edge pulls the next value from every line that has nothing patched to its own first jack
A rising edge sends that line's expression back to its beginning
The clock for that line; each rising edge pulls the next value from its expression, and with nothing patched here the line follows the master clock jack instead
On a clock expression, a second clock whose rising edges also pull the next value; on a pitch expression, a pitch added to what that line puts out, a volt shifting it an octave
Leans the random sequence types; the voltage is divided by 5 and then multiplied by the Bias knob, so with a cable here the knob acts as an attenuverter and a centred knob means no bias at all

outputs.text: That line's output: 10V triggers on a clock expression, and a volt-per-octave pitch on a pitch expression
A 10V pulse each time that line's expression reaches its end and starts again

notes: no line does anything until an expression is typed into its display and compiled by pressing Enter, and until that line is clocked, either at its own first jack or at the master clock.
the expression displays cannot be reached from this help. Click one to type in it, Enter compiles that line, Ctrl and Enter compiles them all, and Escape stops one.
in a pitch expression a value is volt per octave, so 12 gives 1V and c4 gives 0V; in a clock expression it is the number of clock pulses a step lasts, and 0 or less is a rest.
changing an expression while it is running does not interrupt it: the new one takes over when the old one reaches its end.
menu: Run on start up — sets whether the expressions start running as soon as the patch is loaded
Examples — lists a few working expressions to copy
Sequence types — lists the leading characters that set how a sequence is read: forward, backward, ping-pong, shuffle, random, random excluding the last pick, and random walk
Modulators — lists the trailing modulators that set how long a sequence runs before it hands back
Values — lists the two ways a value can be written, as a number or as a pitch letter with an optional sharp, flat and octave
Shortcuts — lists the keys that compile and stop expressions
